summary.headline: Novus Loyalty H1 FY27 revenue reached about ₹98 crore, up roughly 35-40% YoY from ₹71 crore, with AutoPay (80.87% stake) acquisition pending.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue was stated as about ₹98 crore against about ₹71 crore in H1 FY26, with management citing 35-40% growth across revenue lines. The company signed an SPA to acquire 80.87% of AutoPay, a payments business, for a valuation of around ₹130 crore, with roughly ₹40 crore of payment due in June 2027. Management guided H2 FY27 to be in line with or better than H1, and set a consolidated revenue target of ₹500 crore for FY29 and ₹600-650 crore for FY30. Working-capital build-up (unbilled work, inventory of vouchers) was flagged in Q&A.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~₹71 crore in H1 FY26; ~35-40% overall growth as stated

financial_highlights.metric: H2 FY26 revenue (as cited by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: compared with ₹71 crore in H1 FY27
PAT more than ₹14 crore; EBITDA ~₹23 crore

financial_highlights.value: Technology ~100% net; redemption ~16-18%; merchant promotion ~100%; vouchers ~5-7%

segments.name: Technology / platform
segments.commentary: About 7% of gross revenue; ~₹9.5 crore revenue cited, ~90% from SaaS and ~10% on-premise. Management describes it as fully net revenue.

segments.name: Redemption engine
segments.commentary: About 39% of gross revenue; ~₹36 crore in H1 FY27 at ~16-18% gross margin. Central Bank of India onboarding adds low-value, high-frequency redemptions.

segments.name: Merchant promotion
segments.commentary: About 6% of gross revenue; ~₹5 crore in H1 FY27, ~37% growth. Management expects this line to drive the highest profit share.

segments.name: Digital vouchers / gift vouchers
segments.commentary: About 48% of gross revenue; ~₹49 crore in H1 FY27, ~45% growth. Gross margin only 5-7% without a PPI licence.

segments.name: AutoPay (proposed acquisition)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ~₹102 crore, PAT more than ₹14 crore (vs ~₹21.9% margin earlier, now ~13.8%). Management targets 17-20% PAT margin long term and 15-20% organic growth.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Dubai subsidiary set up; two Africa banks onboarded via partners (~$200,000 billed so far); Saudi ~$100,000 technology revenue. FY27 international revenue guided to ~₹7-8 crore.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to be in line with H1 FY27, if not higher.
International revenue ~₹7-8 crore in FY27 (Dubai/Saudi); ~₹12-15 crore minimum from UAE/Middle East next year; Africa ~$400,000 this year; Dubai ~$1 million this year and $2 million next year.
US and Australia expected to contribute ~$1 million in next financial year, subject to a local subsidiary or partner.
Consolidated revenue target ~₹500 crore by FY29 and ₹600-650 crore by FY30.
AutoPay: organic growth 15-20% per year, PAT margin 17-20% long term; PPI licence expected via AutoPay.
Central Bank of India contract (~₹88 crore gross over 5 years) estimated at ~₹3-4 crore net revenue in year one, roughly doubling annually.
Noxcy AI cost expected to break even in 1.5-2 years; AI agents to be monetised separately later.
capex_capacity: AutoPay acquisition: 80.87% stake via SPA; ~20% through share swap, ~₹40 crore from internal accruals and IPO proceeds, and ~₹40-45 crore due June 2027, to be funded partly by a preferential issue.
AutoPay margin pressure attributed to R&D and minimum monthly guarantee (MMG) payments to DMRC; ~₹1.5 crore paid on MMGs.
Company stated to be debt-free and profitable for last four years.
Plans for a small US subsidiary or acquisition of a small digital agency to serve US clients.
Working capital: unbilled work-in-progress ~₹2 crore (NPCI and Bank of Abyssinia), unbilled redemption and merchant promotion revenue, and voucher inventory bought but not sold.
demand_pricing: Management says loyalty market is growing at ~15% CAGR globally (~$17 billion in 2025 to over $51 billion by 2034) and India's market is ~$4 billion, expected to roughly double by 2034.
Around 100 enterprise customers and over 5 crore customers; ~150 crore transactions processed monthly (as stated).
Seasonality is limited: summer ~5-10% uplift, Diwali ~2-5%, New Year a bit higher. Management attributed the lower H2 FY26 to client-driven campaign timing.
Direct competitor in Indian PSU bank RFPs: Billdesk-owned Loyalty Rewards. International competitors: GIIFT, Concilion, Vernost.
Bank of Abyssinia contract $400,000 (about $140,000 billed); Bank of Sparkle about $50,000 billed.
Most clients on SaaS (~90%); NPCI and some banks still on-premise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AutoPay PAT margin fall from ~21.9% to ~13.8%, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed heavy R&D and MMG payments to DMRC for the Saathi app; FY26 revenue was ~₹102 crore with PAT over ₹14 crore (could have been ₹17-18 crore). Long-term PAT margin guided at 17-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the ~₹130 crore valuation and AutoPay growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Valuation was based on a fair-value exercise and negotiation with sellers, with PAT generation as a factor. Management expects AutoPay to grow at least 15-20% YoY and is bidding for an Indian Railways transit loyalty system.

qa_highlights.question: Which verticals will drive higher revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross revenue will rise most in redemption and vouchers, but PAT margin is expected to come mainly from merchant promotion, as systems mature and transaction volumes grow.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality, and why was H2 FY26 lower than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: No material seasonality; campaign timing is client-driven rather than seasonal. H2 FY26 was ~₹56 crore vs ~₹71 crore in H1 FY27 per analyst.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic CAGR for the base business excluding AutoPay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave ~15% for the base business and said AutoPay organic growth could be 15-20% by onboarding new clients such as Confirm Ticket and MakeMyTrip for refund-related use cases.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory/unbilled work up in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix of unbilled work-in-progress (~₹2 crore, NPCI and Bank of Abyssinia, awaiting POs), unbilled redemption revenue, unbilled merchant promotion income (30-45 day return window), and gift voucher inventory bought but not sold.

risks_watch: AutoPay margin compression (~13.8% vs 21.9% earlier) and the timing of DMRC revenue ramp-up.
Working-capital build-up: unbilled work, PO delays, and voucher inventory, with management saying inventory will rise as business grows.
Dependence on a few enterprise clients and banks; client-driven campaign timing causes lumpy quarters.
Execution risk on international expansion: US/Australia need a subsidiary or local partner; BFSI clients there are hesitant to contract with an Indian firm.
Gift voucher margins (5-7%) depend on obtaining a PPI licence through AutoPay; licence not yet secured.
Funding of ~₹40-45 crore due June 2027 and dependence on a preferential issue; figures were given approximately during the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, international expansion, and the AutoPay thesis, with a long-term 2029-2030 target. Answers were less precise on AutoPay margins, the funding split, and the organic CAGR, and the call had audio and question-reading issues.
key_quotes: We always believe in a mix of organic and inorganic growth.
H2 expectations, will be 100% aligned with H1, right?
So, 88 crore is, you can segregate it into two parts, and then divide it into 5 years.

growth.why: H1 FY27 revenue ~₹98 Cr vs ~₹71 Cr (about 35-40% growth), with H2 FY27 guided in line with H1 (~₹98 Cr, flat-ish, not a numeric growth guide) plus ~₹7-8 Cr international revenue and a ₹500 Cr FY29 target; backing is new international markets, the Central Bank of India contract and voucher/redemption demand, but no capacity additions or firm order-book numbers were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: AutoPay PAT margin fell to ~13.8% from ~21.9% on R&D and DMRC MMG payments (~₹1.5 crore paid), with management targeting 17-20% long term; no near-term margin guide given, and the redemption/voucher mix (5-7% and 16-18% gross margins) caps consolidated margin lift.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or capacity additions were discussed; the growth story rests on international entry, the AutoPay acquisition and client onboarding.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue ~₹98 crore vs ~₹71 crore (about 35-40% growth), H2 FY27 guided in line with or above H1, ~150 crore transactions a month, and international revenue of ~₹7-8 crore guided for FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was given; the ~₹40-45 crore AutoPay payment due June 2027 and plans for a US subsidiary or digital agency acquisition are firm cash commitments, but they are acquisitions, not capacity capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided H2 FY27 to be in line with or better than H1 (~₹98 crore) and set FY29 ~₹500 crore and FY30 ₹600-650 crore targets, but H2 FY26 was only ~₹56 crore, so the flat-to-up guide is not yet proven.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Lumpy client-driven campaign timing, unbilled work-in-progress of ~₹2 crore awaiting POs, voucher inventory build, and the PPI licence not yet secured could push revenue or margins below guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI agents (Noxcy) to be monetised later, a PPI licence via AutoPay is expected, and international launches are planned: Dubai ~$1 million this year and $2 million next year, US/Australia ~$1 million next year subject to subsidiary or partner.

rows.label: International revenue ramp (Middle East, Africa, US/Australia)
rows.why: International revenue guided at ~₹7-8 crore in FY27 and ~₹12-15 crore minimum from UAE/Middle East next year, with Dubai at $1 million this year and $2 million next year.

rows.label: AutoPay acquisition and DMRC / Railways ramp
rows.why: Acquisition of 80.87% via SPA at ~₹130 crore valuation, with management expecting AutoPay to grow 15-20% a year and bidding for an Indian Railways transit loyalty system, though the DMRC revenue ramp timing is unclear.

rows.label: Working-capital build-up (unbilled work, voucher inventory)
rows.why: Unbilled WIP of ~₹2 crore plus unbilled redemption and merchant promotion income and unsold voucher inventory; management says inventory will rise as the business grows.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, international expansion and the 2029-30 targets, but was less precise on AutoPay margins, the funding split and the organic CAGR; analysts pushed on the H2 FY26 dip, the AutoPay margin fall and working capital, and the call had audio and question-reading issues.
